data.title: Animate scene controls without requiring components
data.body:
User result: Animate every declared numeric control from the Inspector, whether it belongs to a scene or a component. Scene structure must not disable animation.
Why now: User encounters "Animation requires a component-based scene" during normal creative work. LUX-135 exposes the button but retains this restriction.
Acceptance:
- Use the same animation editor for scene and component controls, including exposed aliases.
- Preserve base values, reset, animation settings, save/reopen, playback and stale-runtime guards.
- Demonstrate a non-component scene and a component scene in the actual app, including save/reopen and invalid-edit preservation.
- Update the shipped authoring skill and validate/install it when behavior changes.
Checklist: implementation; focused regression checks; independent code and UI review; integration; real app demonstration.
Approved in task 01a0a7bb-ee60-76f1-bcd6-5d179614f551. Extend existing animation behavior rather than introduce a second animation system.
data.summary:
Scene and component controls use the same animation editor. Flat scene bindings use the declared schema identity; base values remain independently editable and saved. Incompatible bindings stay disabled rather than retargeting. Display-only animation samples use the existing bounded UI update cadence.
Source: 0ae299d6671a7687e41811f95d9c673d4c3a378d.
Independent review and integration pending.

data.qa:
Demonstrated: build a flat SDK0.2 sphere; Animate Spike height; see changing effective value and unchanged base; save/open the scene; reject invalid code and retain the working preview; build component composition and animate its Scene alias.
Remaining: independent review, main integration, source skill installation/check and combined desktop packaging. No installed-app upgrade is claimed yet. Legacy SDK0.1 is covered by worker/service/persistence checks; actual new native scene demonstration uses SDK0.2.
